channel.title: Economy
channel.description: Find the latest economic news, current events and headlines, as well as blogs and video from CNBC.com.

item.title: Consumer sentiment is in the dumps despite a solid economy. Goldman Sachs blames 'lower happiness'
item.description: Goldman economist Joseph Briggs said broader pessimism in society may be contributing to struggling consumer sentiment even as the economy chugs along.

item.title: Why Japan’s markets flipped the usual script after central bank rate hike
item.description: The yen weakened past 157 against the dollar, the yield on the 10-year Japanese Government Bond slipped, while the Nikkei 225 gained 1.5%.

item.title: Bank of England defies Fed’s rate-hike lead, leaving rates unchanged
item.description: The Bank of England kept rates steady Thursday, even after U.K. inflation rose to 3.1% and energy costs put pressure on prices.

item.title: 'Science fiction': Transport companies — the backbone of economy — are sounding alarm on fuel prices
item.description: Prices for diesel, the fuel type used to power trucks and trains, came in at an all-time high of $6.31 per gallon on Wednesday.

item.title: Consumers hit by one-two punch of oil and rates from Iran war. The estimated bill is $1,700 per household
item.description: Rising oil prices and Treasury yields are lifting energy and borrowing costs for U.S. households, pushing consumers to draw more heavily on savings.

item.title: UK inflation jumps to 3.1% as energy costs soar
item.description: The reading comes a day before the Bank of England updates its monetary policy.

item.title: Indonesia's new finance minister faces an uphill battle on fiscal credibility
item.description: Nazara, sworn in hours after Purbaya's dismissal, spent seven years as deputy finance minister and led the ministry's fiscal policy agency from 2015 to 2019.

item.title: Why de-dollarization discussions are more talk, less action
item.description: BRICS leaders have asserted the need to use local currencies in intra-BRICS trade to cut dependency on dollar.

item.title: Counting the votes: Warsh faces a tough battle as the Fed girds for expected interest rate hike
item.description: Traders were pricing in a better than 92% probability of a rate increase, as well as a more than 75% chance for another one in December.

item.title: Inflation is outpacing wage growth again, squeezing Americans’ paychecks
item.description: In August, consumer prices rose 3.4% over the past year while wages increased just 3.1%.

item.title: Consumer outlook plunges in September as inflation outlook worsens
item.description: The survey's headline index hit a level of 47.8, down 7.5% from the August reading and off 13.2% from a year ago.

item.title: Record U.S. cyclosporiasis outbreak is over, CDC says
item.description: The largest outbreak, linked to shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms, sickened more than 12,000 people.

item.title: Inflation persisted in August, potentially locking in a Fed interest rate hike
item.description: The all-items consumer price index was expected to rise 0.4% in August, with core, excluding food and energy, showing a 0.2% gain, according to the Dow Jones consensus.

item.title: Friday's CPI inflation report is even more important than usual. Here's what to expect
item.description: The Bureau of Labor Statistics will release the August consumer price index report at 8:30 a.m.

item.title: The likelihood of a Fed interest rate hike next week just got a lot higher
item.description: Traders pushed chances for a rate increase to 70% in morning action.

item.title: Wholesale prices rose 0.4% in August, as expected
item.description: The producer price index was expected to rise 0.4% in August, according to the Dow Jones consensus forecast.

item.title: U.S. reveals import ban on slew of Canadian goods as trade war escalates
item.description: Import bans on motorbikes, alcohol and dairy products are due to come into effect on Sept. 29 as the rift between the countries deepens.

item.title: Canada's retaliatory tariffs worth CA$27.6 billion take effect as trade rift with U.S. deepens
item.description: Duties on Canadian imports of U.S. steel and aluminum products have doubled to 50% as a trade war between Washington and Ottawa intensifies.

item.title: China's imports in August miss estimates as calls for rebalancing trade grow
item.description: China's exports and imports gathered momentum in August, as the world's second-largest economy faces mounting pressure to rebalance trade.

item.title: Japan's foreign reserves drop by a record $80 billion in August following yen intervention
item.description: Finance ministry data showed that Japan's official foreign reserves stand at $1.207 trillion, down from July's figure of $1.287 trillion.

item.title: Trump turns up the heat on Warsh as Fed rate hike looms
item.description: Ten days ahead of the next Federal Reserve meeting, the Trump administration looks to be in a full-court press to halt a rate hike in its tracks.

item.title: From ‘mystery vacations’ to hostels, budget travelers get thrifty as prices rise
item.description: Despite rising prices and the travel industry focusing on the luxury segment, budget-minded vacationers are still finding ways to get away.

item.title: Women accounted for almost all of job gains in August. Here's why
item.description: Women accounted for virtually all of August's payroll gains, the latest sign of their growing power in the labor market.

item.title: U.S. payrolls rose 162,000 in August, much more than expected; unemployment rate at 4.1%
item.description: Nonfarm payrolls were expected to increase by 53,000 in August while the unemployment rate held at 4.1%, according to the Dow Jones consensus.

item.title: The big business of personal protection: How private security became a $50 billion industry
item.description: Private security spending and guard employment have climbed as companies and communities respond to high-profile attacks, even as violent crime falls.

item.title: The big August jobs report is due out Friday. Here's what to expect for what has been a jobless summer
item.description: August nonfarm payrolls are expected to rise by 53,000 as a subdued labor market keeps Fed attention focused on inflation.

item.title: Fed Governor Waller indicates he will support holding rates steady at September meeting
item.description: In remarks that seem to contrast with statements last week from Chairman Kevin Warsh, Waller expressed confidence in the current inflation trends.

item.title: 'Danger zone of extreme weather': UN warns of supersized El Niño set to hit global economy and markets
item.description: Latest modeling shows high risks of floods, drought and extreme heat persisting until February 2027.

item.title: South Korea's semiconductor exports just tripled year-over-year. Is it too much of a good thing?
item.description: If growth were to slow in the semiconductor sector, would the slowdown take the Korean economy with it?

item.title: Private payrolls rose by 38,000 in August, less than expected, ADP reports
item.description: Though job creation held positive, August was the smallest gain since January and reflective of a broader slowdown in the labor market.
